response: Yes, reports of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain are related to somatisation. Somatisation refers to the tendency to experience and report psychological distress as physical symptoms. In the context of chronic oro-facial pain, somatisation can manifest as an exaggerated reporting of mechanical dysfunction, such as jaw clicking or locking, even when objective measurements do not support these claims. Studies have shown that individuals with chronic oro-facial pain who exhibit higher levels of somatisation tend to report more severe mechanical dysfunction, despite similar levels of actual mechanical impairment as those with lower somatisation levels. This suggests that psychological factors, such as anxiety and stress, can contribute to the perception and reporting of mechanical dysfunction in chronic oro-facial pain.
